properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 16 at 1:55AM EDT until September 16 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
FFWIWX

The National Weather Service in Northern Indiana has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Grant County in central Indiana...
Northwestern Blackford County in east central Indiana...
Southern Adams County in northeastern Indiana...
Southern Wells County in northeastern Indiana...

* Until 500 AM EDT.

* At 155 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marion, Bluffton, Gas City, Berne, Upland, Montpelier, Geneva, Van
Buren, Nottingham, Poneto, Vera Cruz, Keystone, Dillman, Wellsburg,
Mount Zion, Liberty Center, Travisville, Petroleum and Reiffsburg.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. Showers will continue through the
end of the week, with the bulk of the rainfall expected through
Thursday morning. Storm total rainfall during this time will be
around 0.50" to 1.00". It has been very wet lately and this
amount of rain has the potential to bring the Chena and Little
Chena Rivers above minor flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 106.

* WHERE...Portions of North and Central Texas along and east of the
I-35 corridor.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.
